query: Check accessibility-checker/test-page.html for WCAG AA problems.
expected_behavior: Serves the file over a local http server and opens it in Chrome rather than only reading the HTML source
Runs audit.js in the page and confirms leads with screenshots before reporting them

Reports the planted failures: low-contrast text, missing alt, unlabelled field, placeholder-only label, click-only span, outline removed, positive tabindex, aria-hidden focusable link, invalid role, missing lang, zoom blocked, endless ticker and timed carousel with no pause
Reports nothing from the 'Correct things' section
Writes accessibility-audit/findings.json in the format from findings-format.md, builds it with build_report.py, and opens accessibility-report.html
Puts colour, wording and motion choices into decisions with a recommended option, and code-only changes (div to button, role typo, tabindex, zoom) into fixes with no decision
Doesn't change the audited page's code during the audit

query: Is the homepage of my site keyboard accessible? It's running at http://localhost:5173/
expected_behavior: Uses the running dev server address instead of starting a new server
Walks the page with real Tab key presses, calling __a11yFocusInfo() and taking a screenshot at each stop
Checks focus visibility, order, obscured focus, traps, skip link, and Enter/Space/Escape/arrow-key behaviour on menus and dialogs
Tries every not-keyboard-reachable and pointer-not-focusable lead by hand
Says how many Tab stops were covered if it didn't walk all of them

query: Our marketing site has a hero carousel and a news ticker. Do they pass WCAG?
expected_behavior: Asks for or finds the site address before testing
Runs __a11yMotionSnapshot(), waits about 6 seconds without interacting, then runs __a11yMotionCompare()
Applies the 2.2.2 test: starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds, alongside other content, and no keyboard-operable named pause/stop/hide control
Uses any pause control with the keyboard and confirms the motion actually stops
Treats prefers-reduced-motion support as a recommendation, not a substitute for a pause control
